title: National Taxpayer Advocate 2024 Annual Report to Congress: Most Serious Problem 1, Employee Retention Credit

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the PDF text.

publisher: National Taxpayer Advocate / Taxpayer Advocate Service (IRS)
source_type: Government advocate report section (Most Serious Problem) with IRS administrative data
reliability: Government document by the National Taxpayer Advocate, an office inside the IRS that by statute advocates for taxpayers and reports to Congress; it is an advocate, so it emphasizes taxpayer harm, and it cites IRS data and TAS information requests rather than independent measurement.
findings: The IRS imposed a moratorium on processing new ERC claims on Sept. 14, 2023 to separate valid from invalid claims; the Advocate says bad actors misled business owners about eligibility.

As of Oct. 26, 2024, about 1.2 million ERC claims remained unprocessed (IRS AM RAD report, COVID Business Credits); the section also states about 98 percent of the slightly over one million unprocessed claims were over 120 days old, versus about five percent before the moratorium.

The Advocate states that while waiting, businesses have been forced to close, experienced significant financial hardship, or taken out loans that continue to accrue interest. This is a general statement; the section does not quantify closures.
The Advocate states the IRS provided little to no information on status and that its disallowance notices were confusing and omitted critical information.
limitations: Exact publication date not stated; upload path indicates December 2024. Dated: IRS inventory as of Oct. 26, 2024; the 2025 report shows the backlog subsequently largely cleared.

Advocate advocacy document; the hardship statements are not quantified and the document acknowledges many claims were improper, so affected-business counts for legitimate small businesses are unknown.
Only the introductory sections and selected figures were read in detail.
